items: The FA Cup is the oldest national football competition in the world. The first final was played in 1872.
The marathon's 26.2 miles comes from the 1908 London Olympics course, which ran from Windsor Castle to the stadium at White City.
Basketball was invented by James Naismith in 1891. The first baskets were peach baskets.
Volleyball was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan in Massachusetts.
Yellow tennis balls were first used at Wimbledon in 1986.
The Tour de France was first held in 1903.
The penalty kick was introduced to football in 1891.
A standard darts bullseye hangs 5 ft 8 in above the floor, and the throw line is 7 ft 9¼ in from the board.
Table tennis balls are 40 mm in diameter.
The Boat Race is rowed over the 4.2-mile Championship Course on the Thames, from Putney to Mortlake.
The first Oxford–Cambridge Boat Race was rowed at Henley in 1829.
Legend has it that rugby began in 1823 when William Webb Ellis picked up the ball and ran with it at Rugby School.
The Ashes urn is said to contain the ashes of a burnt cricket bail.
Snooker is said to have been invented by British army officers in India in the 1870s.
A maximum break in snooker is 147: fifteen reds with fifteen blacks, then all six colours.
The highest three-dart checkout in darts is 170: treble 20, treble 20, bullseye.
The first Wimbledon Championships, in 1877, was a men's singles event only.
A cricket over has six balls.
A rugby union team has 15 players; rugby league teams have 13.
An Olympic swimming pool is 50 metres long.
The Olympic flag's five rings were designed by Pierre de Coubertin and first flown at the 1920 Antwerp Games.
The modern Olympic Games began in Athens in 1896.
The Football League, the world's first football league, kicked off on 8 September 1888.
The Premier League's first matches were played on 15 August 1992.
Golf's rules allow a maximum of 14 clubs in the bag.
